title: Linear-factor conjecture for semi-external chambers of vector partition functions
statement:
Let $A$ be a $d \times n$ integer matrix of rank $d$, let $f$ be a facet of $\operatorname{pos}_{\mathbb{R}}(A)$ with inner facet normal $\bm{\iota}$, and let $\gamma$ be a semi-external chamber of $A$ intersecting $f$ $(d-1)$-dimensionally. Assume that $\bm{\iota} \cdot \mathbf{c}=1$ for every column $\mathbf{c}$ of $A$ not on $f$, and that the chamber polynomial $p_A^{\gamma}(\mathbf{y})$ is a polynomial. Let $k$ be the number of columns of $A$ not on $f$. **Linear-factor conjecture.** For every chamber of $A$ intersecting $f$ $(d-1)$-dimensionally, the corresponding polynomial $p_A^{\gamma}(\mathbf{y})$ has the linear factors

$$
(\bm{\iota} \cdot \mathbf{y})+i
$$

for $i=1,\dots,k-1$. The conjecture proposes a generalization of the unimodular linear-factor theorem to suitable non-unimodular matrices, where the dot-product condition controls the factors.
source_name: Stefan Trandafir, “External columns and chambers of vector partition functions”, arXiv:2307.13112 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13112

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).
